stories.title: Louisville survives Kentucky
stories.summary: Louisville defeated Kentucky 30–27 in Week 13, improving to 11–1. Howard won his in-state rivalry matchup by three points, continuing the Cardinals' post–North Carolina winning streak.
stories.people: Joshawn Howard, Nate Sheppard, Dante Moore
stories.beat: Louisville is now in its Week 14 bye before conference championship games; the Kentucky result stands as the regular-season finale.

stories.title: The Loss That Changed the Season
stories.summary: After a 35–28 Week 9 loss against North Carolina, Louisville won four consecutive games: Stanford, California, Boston College, and Kentucky.
stories.beat: What did the players learn from the defeat? Actual game turning points remain unverified.

stories.title: Dante Moore: Freedom vs. Control
stories.summary: Howard calls offensive plays but has given Moore freedom to use installed pre-snap checks. Moore is 92 OVR in the latest extracted roster. Their trust is an ongoing narrative.
stories.beat: How will Moore respond when a high-stakes check fails or succeeds?

stories.title: Nate Sheppard and the Weight of a Program
stories.summary: Sheppard is 99 OVR in the current save. He has openly embraced responsibility in our established dialogue, while Howard insists the offense cannot depend on one player.
stories.beat: Leadership, workload and sharing attention with the quarterback.

stories.title: DJ Waller Jr.: Corner to Starting Safety
stories.summary: Howard moved Waller from cornerback to starting strong safety. His database record still shows CB (84 OVR); the exact save depth chart has not been decoded.
stories.beat: Trust, communication and making the back end his own.

stories.title: Colton Phares Sets the Tone
stories.summary: Phares was responsible for the opening-play forced-fumble recovery touchdown against Virginia. Howard has relied on him to lead front-seven communication.
stories.beat: Can an emotional defensive leader balance intensity with discipline?

stories.title: Landry, Scott and the Turnover Spotlight
stories.summary: Against Virginia, Lesean Landry scored twice on interception returns and Brycen Scott once. Howard warned them not to chase highlights at the expense of assignments.
stories.people: Lesean Landry, Brycen Scott, DJ Waller Jr.
stories.beat: A potential friendly competition—not a verified feud—over big plays and defensive leadership.

stories.title: Lawayne McCoy Wants the Ball
stories.summary: McCoy caught a 66-yard touchdown against Virginia. He wants downfield opportunities, while Howard emphasizes balance and blocking away from the ball.
stories.beat: The line between confidence and impatience can become a story.

stories.title: Anthony Pyke and the Two-Sided Play-Caller
stories.summary: Joshawn Howard personally calls every offensive and defensive play. DC Anthony Pyke coordinates defensive scouting, drilling, game-planning and communication, and advises Howard.
stories.beat: A demanding partnership built on honest feedback.

stories.title: Joshawn Howard vs. Rich Rodriguez
stories.summary: Rodriguez gave Howard his college coaching opportunity at West Virginia. Howard later returned as Louisville HC and won 31–24 at West Virginia in Week 1.
stories.beat: Respect and competition without manufacturing a personal feud.

stories.title: Virginia: The First Loss, Then Revenge
stories.summary: Virginia handed Howard his first college football loss. His Louisville team defeated Virginia 59–21 in Week 4, including four defensive touchdowns.
stories.people: Joshawn Howard, Colton Phares, Lesean Landry, Brycen Scott
stories.beat: A rivalry that helped shape Howard’s approach to emotion and preparation.

stories.title: Death Valley: 14–7
stories.summary: The save confirms Louisville beat Clemson 14–7 in Week 5. The earlier coaching plan was balanced offense, controlled-aggression defense and disciplined communication.
stories.beat: A hard-fought scoreline, not a verified drive-by-drive defensive narrative.

stories.title: Boston College: Two-Point Escape
stories.summary: Louisville won 31–29 in Week 12. The exact winning sequence and statistical leaders are not decoded, so nobody receives invented credit for a specific play.
stories.beat: Narrow victory could fuel urgency ahead of Kentucky.

stories.title: Stanford: A 48–45 Thriller
stories.summary: Louisville’s 48–45 victory over Stanford in Week 10 is save-verified. We do not know whether the result involved a late comeback or overtime.
stories.beat: High-scoring volatility versus Howard’s expectation of composure.

stories.title: From West Virginia’s Big 12 Title to Louisville
stories.summary: With Rich Rodriguez at West Virginia, Howard helped win the Big 12 and reach the national championship, where WVU lost to BYU 24–7. He accepted Louisville’s HC job and finished WVU’s postseason.
stories.beat: The foundation of Howard’s head-coaching identity.

stories.title: Woodford County Roots
stories.summary: Howard’s path began at Woodford County High School, coaching alongside Dennis Johnson. His Kentucky ties add weight to the next rivalry but do not establish a Louisville–Kentucky game result.
stories.beat: Returning to his home-state football roots.

pressQuestions.text: Coach Howard, Louisville escaped Kentucky 30–27. With your ties to the state, what does this rivalry win mean to your players?
options: Our guys earned it. They stayed together when the game got close.
A rivalry win matters, but we have plenty to correct after a three-point finish.
I know what this game means on both sides. Our players got the job done for Louisville.

pressQuestions.text: Four wins in a row since the North Carolina loss. Has this team learned how to handle adversity?
options: You find out who you are in games like this. They've grown.
We're 11–1, but our standards are higher than simply surviving.
Nobody outside this building knows the work our players put in.

pressQuestions.text: You call both offense and defense. How do you evaluate your own performance in a three-point rivalry game?
options: Every call is my responsibility. We'll study the film and own the corrections.
Anthony Pyke and this staff prepared us. The decisions are still mine.
We'll learn from this, because the next game won't get easier.

officeScenes.title: Recover and Evaluate
scene: Howard
We finished the regular season 11–1. There is no game this week, but there is still work to do.
Pyke
We can heal up or dig into the film. Both matter going into championship season.
officeScenes.prompt: What does Howard prioritize on the first day of the bye?
options: Treatment, rest and a light walkthrough.
Grade recent close games and identify recurring errors.
Moore, Sheppard, Phares and Waller assess where the team stands.

responses.A: The training staff gets a clear recovery plan. Veterans appreciate the rest; Howard demands a sharp return.
responses.B: Howard and Pyke build an honest correction list. Players see that 11–1 does not excuse mistakes.
responses.C: The four leaders take ownership of preparation and morale. Howard listens before setting the week's priorities.

officeScenes.title: Study the Field
scene: Moore
We don't know the opponent yet, Coach. How do we prepare for the possibilities?
Howard
By staying ready without pretending the matchup has already been decided.
options: Separate film breakdowns for potential conference championship and playoff opponents.
Focus on red zone, two-minute drives and conversion downs regardless of opponent.
Practice multiple approaches without committing to a matchup.

responses.A: The staff divides scouting assignments. The players keep working on their own execution.
responses.B: Moore, Sheppard and the defense rehearse pressure situations. Howard owns every live play call.
responses.C: Howard installs answers for multiple defensive looks while keeping the offense balanced.

officeScenes.title: Protect the Stars
scene: Sheppard
Coach, I'm ready to work. Don't hold me out just because it's a bye.
Howard
We have to balance being ready against being worn down.
officeScenes.prompt: How does Howard handle player workload?
options: Keep starters sharp with controlled work and give backups meaningful reps.
Maintain full-speed competitive practice with managed contact.
Tailor workloads by position and player, with trainers involved.

responses.A: Sheppard gets fewer reps but works closely with the younger backs. The depth chart gets attention.
responses.B: The veterans appreciate the intensity. Pyke monitors fatigue and Howard reminds everyone to avoid unnecessary contact.
responses.C: The staff sets individual practice plans. Moore, Sheppard and the defensive captains each receive clear goals.

officeScenes.title: Championship Identity
scene: Pyke
Our defense will need answers for explosive plays when the stakes rise.
Phares
Then make us earn every alignment in practice.
Howard
We build a plan without guessing who we'll face.
options: Four-man pressure, disguised coverages and reliable tackling.
Balance the run and pass with selective shots and installed quarterback checks.
Practice clock management, fourth downs and late-game calls on both sides.

responses.A: Phares and Waller lead the checks. Pyke prepares the defense while Howard makes every play call.
responses.B: Moore and Sheppard work through flexible concepts; Howard retains play-calling control.
responses.C: The offense and defense run high-pressure situations. Howard emphasizes decision-making over theatrics.

officeScenes.title: One Message, No Opponent
scene: Reporter
Coach Howard, Louisville is 11–1 heading into the conference championship weekend. How do you keep the team focused during the bye?
officeScenes.prompt: What is Howard's Friday media response?
options: We cannot control the bracket. We can control our preparation.
We've earned a chance to compete for something meaningful, and we intend to be ready.
Records don't win postseason games. Execution does.

responses.A: The message around the program centers on preparation, not projection.
responses.B: Players hear confidence without a made-up opponent. The media highlights Howard's ambitions.
responses.C: Howard's restrained tone reinforces accountability before championship weekend.
